developments: Nvidia reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive, sending its shares up about 30% and the Nasdaq up about 6.6% by mid-morning New York time, CoinDesk and The Block reported.
Bitcoin rose as high as about $64,520 on Kraken after the news and traded near $62,570 at 16:30 UK, up from about $61,470 at the morning edition.
Zcash jumped to about $841 on Kraken at 16:30 UK, up about 7% since the morning, after touching about $907; no single news cause was found.
briefing.changed: Clearly firmer than this morning. The AI-stock rout that drove last week's sell-off partly reversed on the Huang news, lifting bitcoin and crypto shares, though bitcoin gave back about half its spike from the $64,500 high.
briefing.question: Does the tech rebound bring buyers back to spot bitcoin ETFs, after four weeks of outflows, or does bitcoin fade with yields near 4.95% and the dollar at a 20-month high?
briefing.watch: Monday's spot bitcoin ETF flow figures, due Tuesday morning UK, and US PCE inflation on Wednesday at 13:30 UK. The next 🔴 event is the Fed decision on Wednesday 9 December at 19:00 UK.

lead.headline: Bitcoin jumps as Nvidia brings back Huang and tech stocks soar
lead.standfirst: Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as chief executive sparked a sharp rebound in technology shares on Monday, carrying bitcoin briefly above $64,000.
body: Nvidia's board voted unanimously to reinstate Jensen Huang as president, chief executive and director with immediate effect, The Block and CoinDesk reported. The shares rose about 30%, having fallen about 43% in the month after his 12 November resignation, according to The Block.

The news lifted the wider market. The Nasdaq was up about 6.6% and the S&P 500 about 4.7% at 10:42 New York time, CoinDesk's live blog reported, a partial reversal of last week's 10.4% Nasdaq fall that had dragged bitcoin to a two-year low near $55,000.

Bitcoin rose as high as about $64,520 on Kraken, Kraken data showed, before easing to about $62,570 at 16:30 UK, roughly 2% above the morning edition. Zcash traded near $841, about 7% higher on the day after touching about $907.

Not every signal was supportive. CoinDesk reported that the US 10-year Treasury yield rose to 4.95% and that the dollar index reached its highest since March 2025. Strategy, the largest corporate holder, said it bought only 457 BTC last week for $29.6 million, Bitcoin Magazine reported, citing a filing.
The next tests are Monday's spot ETF flow figures, due on Tuesday morning UK time, and October's US PCE inflation data on Wednesday at 13:30 UK, ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.

headline: Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang sparked a tech rally that lifted bitcoin to about $64,500 before it eased to near $62,570. Zcash rose about 7% to around $841.
spoken: Cryptonaire Post, afternoon edition, Monday the twenty third of November. Nvidia has brought back Jensen Huang as chief executive, and tech shares are soaring, with the Nasdaq up more than six percent. Bitcoin briefly topped sixty four thousand dollars and is now near sixty two thousand six hundred, about two percent higher than this morning. Zcash is up about seven percent at around eight hundred and forty dollars. Treasury yields and the dollar are higher, which may limit the rebound. Watch spot bitcoin fund flows tomorrow morning and US inflation data on Wednesday at half past one. The next big event is the Fed decision on the ninth of December at seven in the evening. Information only, not advice.

stories.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang; Nasdaq jumps about 6.6%
stories.why: Nvidia's board unanimously reinstated Huang as CEO, and the shares rose about 30% after a 43% fall over the past month, The Block and CoinDesk reported. The Nasdaq was up about 6.6% at 10:42 New York time, reversing part of the AI-stock rout that pulled bitcoin to a two-year low last week.

note.read: Last week's crypto sell-off was tied to the tech rout, so a tech rebound removes one of the main sources of pressure on bitcoin.
note.alt: A one-day relief rally on one company's news may not last, and the Fed rate-rise path that also weighed on risk assets has not changed.
note.change: The Nasdaq giving back most of today's gain this week would suggest the relief was short-lived.

stories.title: Bitcoin hits about $64,520, then eases to near $62,570
stories.why: Kraken showed bitcoin peaking near $64,520 after the Nvidia news and trading near $62,570 at 16:30 UK, about 2% above the morning edition and some 13% above last week's low near $55,000. The new evidence is that the rebound extended into the US session, though bitcoin gave back about half the spike.

note.read: Bitcoin is trading as a high-beta tech proxy, rising with the Nasdaq.
note.alt: Fading from the high while stocks held their gains may show sellers still using rallies to cut risk.
note.change: A close back below $61,000 would undo today's gain; a hold above $64,500 would mark a new high for the rebound.

stories.title: Zcash rises about 7% to near $841 after touching $907
stories.why: Kraken showed ZEC near $841 at 16:30 UK, up from about $786 at the morning edition, after a day's range of about $775 to $907. The morning's 'no material change' no longer holds; ZEC outpaced bitcoin's rise.
stories.caveat: No specific ZEC news was found to explain the move; it coincided with the broad crypto and tech rally.

note.read: ZEC moved roughly three times as much as bitcoin, consistent with a higher-beta coin in a risk-on session.
note.alt: A fast move to $907 and quick retreat may reflect thin liquidity and short covering rather than lasting demand.
note.change: Confirmed ZEC-specific news, such as a listing or upgrade, would point to more than the market's general rebound.

stories.title: US yields climb and dollar hits 20-month high; PCE due Wednesday
stories.why: CoinDesk's live blog reported the 10-year Treasury yield at 4.95% and the 2-year at 4.70%, with the dollar index at its highest since March 2025. CoinDesk's week-ahead piece put October PCE inflation on Wednesday at 13:30 UK, forecast at 0.3% on the month, with more than 95% pricing a quarter-point December Fed rise.
stories.caveat: The dollar-index level comes from the live blog's headline; the full text could not be checked.

stories.title: UK crypto exchanges barred from market making on their own venues
stories.why: Bitcoin Magazine reported that the FCA's final rules (PS26/11) stop exchange operators trading against their own capital on venues they run from 25 October 2027, while a Treasury order made on 18 November lets outside market makers quote without a separate permission. Firms must apply for authorisation by 28 February 2027, which could change which venues UK users can use and how deep their order books are.

stories.title: Strategy buys just 457 BTC and spends more on buybacks
stories.why: Strategy bought 457 BTC for $29.6 million last week, taking its holdings to 851,305 BTC at an average cost of $75,446, Bitcoin Magazine reported, citing a filing. It spent $211.8 million repurchasing preferred shares, so the biggest corporate buyer is adding far less bitcoin than in past sell-offs.

stories.title: Bitcoin Core discloses node-stall bug, fixed in latest releases
stories.why: Bitcoin Core disclosed a medium-severity bug that let an attacker briefly stall a node's processing, Bitcoin Magazine reported. It is fixed in versions 30.5, 31.3 and 32.1; the 29.x line is end-of-life with no fix. Relevant to anyone running their own node, not to funds held.

stories.title: Elliptic tracks $247 million of Binance hack funds through coinjoins
stories.why: CoinDesk reported, citing Elliptic, that at least $247 million from the $6.3 billion Binance hack passed through coinjoin transactions, with about $2.35 billion still in linked wallets as of 20 November. Large sales of the remaining stolen funds are a potential source of selling, and a court is set to consider frozen assets on 1 December.

explained.title: Why a chip company's boss can move bitcoin
body: Big investors often hold bitcoin and technology shares in the same 'risk' bucket. When a large tech stock like Nvidia crashes, funds cut risk across the board, selling bitcoin too; when it rebounds, the same money tends to flow back.
That link is why bitcoin fell during last week's AI-stock rout and jumped on Monday's Nvidia news. It can fade when crypto-specific forces, such as ETF flows or rate expectations, take over.

investigating: Did ETF buyers return with the tech rally? Evidence: Monday's spot bitcoin ETF flow figures, due Tuesday morning UK.
What drove Zcash's spike to $907? Evidence: an exchange announcement, derivatives liquidation data or a Zcash project update.
Did Chainflip recover its stolen BTC by the 18:38 UK bounty deadline? Evidence: a Chainflip statement or on-chain movement of the 122.9 BTC.
